structures.label: Right atrium
structures.description: Receives blood returning from the body and passes it to the right ventricle.

structures.label: Left atrium
structures.description: Receives oxygen-rich blood from the lungs and passes it to the left ventricle.

structures.label: Ventricular wall
structures.description: Muscular tissue surrounding the two lower pumping chambers of the heart.

structures.label: Right ventricular cavity
structures.description: The space inside the right ventricle, which pumps blood toward the lungs.

structures.label: Left ventricular cavity
structures.description: The space inside the left ventricle, which pumps blood into the aorta.

structures.label: Ascending aorta
structures.description: The aorta carries blood away from the heart to the body.

structures.label: Aortic arch
structures.description: Part of the aorta, the main artery carrying blood from the heart.

structures.label: Pulmonary trunk
structures.description: Carries blood from the right ventricle toward the lungs.

structures.label: Superior vena cava
structures.description: One of the large veins returning blood from the body to the right atrium.

structures.label: Left coronary artery
structures.description: Supplies the heart muscle, including parts of the left heart and ventricular septum.

structures.label: Right coronary artery
structures.description: Supplies the right atrium and parts of both ventricles.

structures.description: The front portion of a cerebral hemisphere; it includes cortical regions involved in planning and voluntary movement.

structures.label: Right frontal lobe
structures.description: The front portion of a cerebral hemisphere; it includes cortical regions involved in planning and voluntary movement.

structures.label: Left parietal lobe
structures.description: A superior-posterior part of a cerebral hemisphere that participates in integrating bodily sensory information.

structures.label: Right parietal lobe
structures.description: A superior-posterior part of a cerebral hemisphere that participates in integrating bodily sensory information.

structures.label: Left temporal lobe
structures.description: A lower lateral part of a cerebral hemisphere that includes regions involved in hearing and memory.

structures.label: Right temporal lobe
structures.description: A lower lateral part of a cerebral hemisphere that includes regions involved in hearing and memory.

structures.label: Left occipital lobe
structures.description: The posterior part of a cerebral hemisphere and the principal cortical region for visual processing.

structures.label: Right occipital lobe
structures.description: The posterior part of a cerebral hemisphere and the principal cortical region for visual processing.

structures.label: Left hippocampus
structures.description: A curved deep structure of the temporal region involved in forming and organizing memories.

structures.label: Right hippocampus
structures.description: A curved deep structure of the temporal region involved in forming and organizing memories.

structures.label: Midbrain
structures.description: The upper portion of the brainstem, between the forebrain and pons.

structures.label: Pons
structures.description: The rounded middle portion of the brainstem, anterior to the cerebellum.

structures.label: Medulla oblongata
structures.description: The lowest portion of the brainstem, continuous inferiorly with the spinal cord.

structures.label: Cerebellum
structures.description: A folded structure behind the brainstem that helps coordinate movement and balance.

structures.label: Left lateral ventricle
structures.description: One of the paired cavities deep in the cerebrum through which cerebrospinal fluid circulates.

structures.label: Right lateral ventricle
structures.description: One of the paired cavities deep in the cerebrum through which cerebrospinal fluid circulates.

structures.label: Third ventricle
structures.description: A narrow midline cavity connected to the lateral ventricles and cerebral aqueduct.

structures.label: Cerebral aqueduct
structures.description: A narrow channel through the midbrain linking the third and fourth ventricles.

structures.label: Fourth ventricle
structures.description: A cavity between the brainstem and cerebellum that receives fluid from the cerebral aqueduct.

structures.description: The windpipe carries air toward the right and left main bronchi.

structures.label: Liver surface
structures.description: The liver processes nutrients, stores energy, and makes bile to help digest fats. It sits beneath the diaphragm, mostly on the right side of the abdomen.

structures.label: Gallbladder
structures.description: A small organ beneath the liver that stores bile between meals and releases it into the small intestine to support fat digestion.

structures.label: Portal vein
structures.description: The hepatic portal vein brings nutrient-rich blood to the liver from the digestive organs. Its branches distribute this blood through the liver.

structures.label: Hepatic veins
structures.description: The hepatic veins carry blood away from the liver toward the inferior vena cava, returning it to the circulation.

structures.label: Hepatic artery
structures.description: The hepatic artery supplies oxygenated blood to the liver, alongside the nutrient-rich blood arriving through the portal vein.

structures.label: Hepatic bile ducts
structures.description: A branching network collects bile from the liver. The right and left hepatic ducts join the common hepatic duct.

structures.label: Cystic duct
structures.description: The cystic duct connects the gallbladder with the bile duct system, providing a passage for stored bile.

structures.label: Right kidney
structures.description: The patient’s right kidney is one of the paired organs that filter blood and produce urine. In this source body it sits slightly lower than the left kidney.

structures.label: Left kidney
structures.description: The patient’s left kidney is shown in its source alignment beside the spine. This surface mesh does not expose cortex, medulla, or the renal pelvis.

structures.label: Right ureter
structures.description: The right ureter is the narrow muscular tube that carries urine from the right kidney toward the bladder. The bladder is outside this release’s represented scope.

structures.label: Left ureter
structures.description: The left ureter descends from the left kidney toward the bladder. Its lower end is truncated here because the bladder is not included in the selected geometry.

structures.label: Right renal artery
structures.description: The right renal artery supplies the right kidney. The source concept combines its represented trunk and mapped branches into one selectable scene object.

structures.label: Left renal artery
structures.description: The left renal artery supplies the left kidney. Color is illustrative and is used to distinguish the arterial meshes from adjacent surfaces.

structures.label: Stomach
structures.description: A muscular J-shaped sac in the upper left abdomen that stores food, mixes it with digestive juices, and passes it on in small amounts.

structures.label: Esophagus (lower part)
structures.description: The muscular tube that carries swallowed food down through the chest. It passes through the diaphragm and opens into the stomach at the cardia.

structures.label: Duodenum
structures.description: The first part of the small intestine. It receives food from the stomach through the pylorus and curves around the head of the pancreas.

structures.label: Celiac trunk
structures.description: A short artery branching from the abdominal aorta. It divides into the left gastric, splenic, and common hepatic arteries, which supply the stomach and its neighbours.

structures.label: Left gastric artery
structures.description: The smallest celiac branch. It runs up toward the esophagus and along the lesser curvature of the stomach.

structures.label: Splenic artery
structures.description: A winding branch running left behind the stomach along the pancreas to the spleen. Its branches also supply parts of the stomach.

structures.label: Common hepatic artery
structures.description: The celiac branch running right toward the liver. Its branches help supply the stomach, duodenum, and pancreas.

structures.label: Spleen
structures.description: An organ of the immune and blood systems that sits behind and to the left of the stomach, under the ribs.

structures.label: Pancreas
structures.description: A gland lying behind the stomach. It releases digestive juices into the duodenum and hormones such as insulin into the blood.

attribution.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science licensed under CC Attribution-Share Alike 2.1 Japan

structures.label: Pancreas
structures.description: A gland behind the stomach. Its head sits in the curve of the duodenum and its tail reaches the spleen.

structures.label: Pancreatic duct
structures.description: Carries digestive juices from the gland along its length and empties them into the duodenum.

structures.label: Duodenum
structures.description: The first part of the small intestine. It curves around the head of the pancreas and receives the pancreatic duct.

structures.label: Spleen
structures.description: An organ in the upper left abdomen. The tail of the pancreas ends near its hilum.

structures.label: Celiac trunk
structures.description: A short branch of the aorta that divides into arteries supplying the stomach, liver, spleen and pancreas.

structures.label: Common hepatic artery
structures.description: Runs from the celiac trunk toward the liver and gives off the gastroduodenal artery.

structures.label: Gastroduodenal artery
structures.description: Passes behind the first part of the duodenum and leads to the arteries around the pancreatic head.

structures.label: Pancreaticoduodenal arteries
structures.description: Arcades around the head of the pancreas that supply it and the duodenum, joining branches from above and below.

structures.label: Splenic artery
structures.description: Runs from the celiac trunk along the upper border of the pancreas to the spleen.

structures.label: Pancreatic branches
structures.description: Branches that supply the neck, body and tail of the pancreas.

structures.label: Superior mesenteric artery
structures.description: Leaves the aorta behind the neck of the pancreas and supplies much of the intestine.

structures.label: Splenic vein
structures.description: Drains the spleen and runs behind the pancreas to join the superior mesenteric vein.

structures.label: Superior mesenteric vein
structures.description: Drains much of the intestine. Its left border marks where the head of the pancreas ends and the body begins.

structures.label: Portal vein
structures.description: Formed behind the neck of the pancreas where the splenic and superior mesenteric veins meet. It carries blood to the liver.

structures.label: Pancreaticoduodenal veins
structures.description: Drain the head of the pancreas and the duodenum toward the portal system.

structures.label: Spleen
structures.description: The largest lymphatic organ. It filters blood, removes worn-out red blood cells, and helps the immune system respond to infection.

structures.label: Splenic artery
structures.description: Carries blood from the celiac trunk along the upper border of the pancreas to the spleen.

structures.label: Splenic vein
structures.description: Drains blood from the spleen behind the pancreas. It joins the superior mesenteric vein to form the portal vein, which carries it to the liver.

structures.label: Celiac trunk
structures.description: A short branch of the abdominal aorta that divides to supply the stomach, liver and spleen. The splenic artery is its largest branch.

structures.label: Superior mesenteric vein
structures.description: Drains the small intestine and joins the splenic vein behind the neck of the pancreas.

structures.label: Stomach
structures.description: Lies in front of and to the right of the spleen. The spleen’s front surface rests against the back of the stomach.

structures.label: Pancreas
structures.description: Its tail reaches toward the splenic hilum, and the splenic vessels run along its upper border and back.

structures.label: Left kidney
structures.description: Sits behind and below the spleen. The spleen’s inner surface touches the upper part of the left kidney.

structures.label: Left adrenal gland
structures.description: A small hormone-producing gland on top of the left kidney, close to the spleen’s inner surface.

attribution.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science licensed under CC Attribution-Share Alike 2.1 Japan

structures.label: Gallbladder
structures.description: A pear-shaped sac on the underside of the liver. It stores and concentrates bile between meals and squeezes it out after eating.

structures.label: Cystic duct
structures.description: A short duct from the neck of the gallbladder. Bile flows in through it to be stored and back out when the gallbladder contracts.

structures.label: Common hepatic duct
structures.description: Formed where the right and left hepatic ducts meet. It carries bile from the liver down toward the duodenum.

structures.label: Right hepatic duct
structures.description: Drains bile from the right part of the liver. It is short in this model.

structures.label: Left hepatic duct
structures.description: Drains bile from the left part of the liver and runs across to meet the right hepatic duct.

structures.label: Intrahepatic bile ducts
structures.description: Branches inside the liver that collect bile from its segments and lead to the right and left hepatic ducts.

structures.label: Pancreatic duct
structures.description: Runs the length of the pancreas. It usually joins the common bile duct just before both open into the duodenum.

structures.label: Liver
structures.description: Makes bile and drains it through the hepatic ducts. The gallbladder lies in a shallow fossa on its underside.

structures.label: Duodenum
structures.description: The first part of the small intestine. Bile and pancreatic juice enter it through the major duodenal papilla.

structures.label: Pancreas
structures.description: A gland behind the stomach. The lower common bile duct passes through or behind its head.

structures.label: Portal vein
structures.description: Carries blood from the gut and spleen to the liver. It runs behind the bile duct and the hepatic artery.

structures.label: Common hepatic artery
structures.description: Runs from the celiac trunk toward the liver and continues as the hepatic artery proper.

structures.label: Hepatic artery proper
structures.description: Climbs beside the bile duct toward the liver and divides into the right and left hepatic arteries.

structures.label: Right hepatic artery
structures.description: Supplies the right part of the liver. The cystic artery to the gallbladder usually arises from it.

structures.label: Left hepatic artery
structures.description: Supplies the left part of the liver.

structures.label: Urinary bladder
structures.description: A hollow, balloon-shaped muscular organ in the pelvis that stores urine until it is released.

structures.label: Right ureter
structures.description: A narrow muscular tube that carries urine from the right kidney down to the bladder.

structures.label: Left ureter
structures.description: A narrow muscular tube that carries urine from the left kidney down to the bladder.

structures.label: Urethra
structures.description: The tube that lets urine leave the body from the bottom of the bladder.

structures.label: Prostate
structures.description: A walnut-sized gland that sits just below the bladder and surrounds the first part of the urethra.

structures.label: Right seminal vesicle
structures.description: A small gland behind the bladder that adds fluid to semen. It lies close to the bladder’s back wall.

structures.label: Left seminal vesicle
structures.description: A small gland behind the bladder that adds fluid to semen. It lies close to the bladder’s back wall.

structures.label: Right pubococcygeus
structures.description: Part of the pelvic floor muscles, which support the bladder and help hold urine in until it is released.

structures.label: Left pubococcygeus
structures.description: Part of the pelvic floor muscles, which support the bladder and help hold urine in until it is released.

structures.label: Right puborectalis
structures.description: Part of the pelvic floor muscles. It forms a sling that loops behind the lower rectum.

structures.label: Left puborectalis
structures.description: Part of the pelvic floor muscles. It forms a sling that loops behind the lower rectum.

structures.label: Rectum
structures.description: The last part of the large intestine, which stores stool. It lies behind the bladder and prostate.

structures.label: Cornea
structures.description: The clear, curved front window of the eye. It lets light in and does most of the focusing.

structures.label: Sclera
structures.description: The tough white outer coat of the eyeball. It protects the eye and anchors the eye muscles.

structures.label: Choroid
structures.description: A layer rich in blood vessels between the sclera and the retina that nourishes the outer retina.

structures.label: Retina
structures.description: The light-sensitive lining at the back of the eye. It turns light into signals sent along the optic nerve.

structures.label: Iris
structures.description: The coloured ring behind the cornea. Its muscles change the size of the pupil to control how much light enters.

structures.label: Anterior chamber
structures.description: The fluid-filled space between the cornea and the iris. Its clear fluid, the aqueous humour, keeps the eye’s shape.

structures.label: Lens
structures.description: A clear, flexible structure behind the iris that fine-tunes focus for near and far objects.

structures.label: Suspensory ligament of lens
structures.description: Fine fibres that hold the lens in place. Changes in their tension let the lens change shape to focus.

structures.label: Vitreous body
structures.description: The clear gel that fills the large space behind the lens and helps hold the eye’s shape.

structures.label: Superior rectus
structures.description: One of the six muscles that move the eye. It mainly turns the eye upward.

structures.label: Inferior rectus
structures.description: One of the six muscles that move the eye. It mainly turns the eye downward.

structures.label: Medial rectus
structures.description: One of the six muscles that move the eye. It turns the eye inward, toward the nose.

structures.label: Lateral rectus
structures.description: One of the six muscles that move the eye. It turns the eye outward, away from the nose.

structures.label: Superior oblique
structures.description: An eye muscle whose tendon passes through a small pulley, the trochlea, before reaching the eyeball. It mainly rotates the eye and helps it look down and out.

structures.label: Inferior oblique
structures.description: An eye muscle that wraps under the eyeball from the front. It mainly rotates the eye and helps it look up and out.

structures.label: Levator palpebrae superioris
structures.description: The muscle that raises the upper eyelid. It does not move the eyeball.

structures.label: Optic nerve
structures.description: Carries visual signals from the retina to the brain.

structures.label: Trochlea
structures.description: A small loop of cartilage that acts as a pulley for the tendon of the superior oblique muscle.

structures.label: Lacrimal gland
structures.description: Makes the watery part of tears, which keep the front of the eye moist and clean.

structures.label: Upper tarsal plate
structures.description: A firm plate of dense connective tissue that stiffens and shapes the upper eyelid.

structures.label: Lower tarsal plate
structures.description: A firm plate of dense connective tissue that supports the lower eyelid.

structures.label: Esophagus
structures.description: A muscular tube about 25 cm long that carries swallowed food from the throat to the stomach. It runs behind the trachea and the heart and passes through the diaphragm.

structures.label: Stomach
structures.description: The esophagus ends just below the diaphragm, which is not shown, by opening into the stomach at the cardia.

structures.label: Trachea
structures.description: The windpipe lies directly in front of the esophagus in the neck and upper chest, until it divides into the two main bronchi.

structures.label: Main bronchi
structures.description: The left main bronchus crosses in front of the esophagus and presses a shallow narrowing into it.

structures.label: Thyroid gland
structures.description: Wraps around the front and sides of the trachea in the lower neck, beside the start of the esophagus.

structures.label: Left atrium
structures.description: The back of the heart. The esophagus lies directly behind it, separated only by the pericardium.

structures.label: Arch of aorta
structures.description: Curves over the left main bronchus, crossing the left side of the esophagus and leaving a narrowing where it presses on it.

structures.label: Descending aorta
structures.description: Runs down behind and to the left of the esophagus. Near the diaphragm the esophagus crosses in front of it.

structures.label: Esophageal arteries
structures.description: Small branches of the aorta that supply the thoracic part of the esophagus.

structures.label: Inferior thyroid arteries
structures.description: Supply the thyroid gland and send branches to the esophagus in the neck.

structures.label: Left gastric artery
structures.description: Runs along the upper curve of the stomach and sends branches up to the abdominal part of the esophagus.

structures.label: Azygos vein
structures.description: Runs up the right side of the spine, behind the esophagus, and drains most of the esophagus in the chest.

structures.label: Hemiazygos veins
structures.description: Run up the left side of the spine and cross behind the aorta to join the azygos vein.

structures.label: Left gastric vein
structures.description: Drains the lower esophagus into the portal system. Its link with the azygos veins is where esophageal varices form when portal pressure rises.

structures.label: Right vagus nerve
structures.description: Descends beside the esophagus, joins the esophageal plexus and passes through the hiatus mostly behind it, as the posterior vagal trunk.

structures.label: Left vagus nerve
structures.description: Crosses the aortic arch, then spreads over the esophagus and passes through the hiatus mostly in front of it, as the anterior vagal trunk.

structures.label: Recurrent laryngeal nerves
structures.description: Branches of the vagus that climb back up in the groove between the trachea and esophagus to reach the larynx.

structures.label: Duodenum
structures.description: The first, C-shaped part of the small intestine. It receives food from the stomach along with bile and pancreatic juices.

structures.label: Jejunum
structures.description: The middle part of the small intestine, where much of the digestion and absorption of nutrients takes place.

structures.label: Ileum
structures.description: The last part of the small intestine. It continues absorbing nutrients and joins the large intestine in the lower right abdomen.

structures.label: Appendix
structures.description: A narrow, finger-shaped pouch that projects from the beginning of the large intestine in the lower right abdomen.

structures.label: Ascending colon
structures.description: Rises along the right side of the abdomen from the start of the large intestine toward the liver. The colon absorbs water and forms stool.

structures.label: Transverse colon
structures.description: Crosses the upper abdomen from right to left, below the liver and stomach.

structures.label: Descending colon
structures.description: Runs down the left side of the abdomen and carries stool toward the rectum.

structures.label: Rectum
structures.description: The final straight section of the large intestine, in the pelvis, which stores stool until it leaves the body through the anus.

structures.label: Mesocolic taenia
structures.description: One of three ribbon-like bands of longitudinal muscle on the colon. It runs along the side where the colon is attached by its mesentery.

structures.label: Omental taenia
structures.description: A band of longitudinal colon muscle that, on the transverse colon, runs where the greater omentum attaches.

structures.label: Free taenia
structures.description: The band of longitudinal colon muscle with no attachment, visible on the front of the ascending and descending colon.

structures.label: Hyoid bone
structures.description: A U-shaped bone above the larynx that touches no other bone. The larynx hangs from it by the thyrohyoid membrane.

structures.label: Thyroid cartilage
structures.description: The largest cartilage of the larynx. Its two plates meet at the front to form the laryngeal prominence, the Adam’s apple, and shield the vocal folds.

structures.label: Cricoid cartilage
structures.description: The only complete ring of cartilage in the airway, narrow at the front and tall at the back. It sits below the thyroid cartilage and on top of the trachea.

structures.label: Epiglottis
structures.description: A leaf-shaped flap of elastic cartilage behind the tongue. It tips back over the entrance of the larynx when you swallow.

structures.label: Arytenoid cartilages
structures.description: Two small pyramids on the back of the cricoid. The vocal ligaments attach to them, so their rocking and sliding opens and closes the vocal folds.

structures.label: Corniculate and cuneiform cartilages
structures.description: Tiny nodules of cartilage. The corniculates cap the arytenoids and the cuneiforms stiffen the aryepiglottic folds at the entrance of the larynx.

structures.label: Thyrohyoid membrane
structures.description: A sheet that hangs the thyroid cartilage from the hyoid bone. It is thickened in the midline and at its back edges into the thyrohyoid ligaments.

structures.label: Median cricothyroid ligament
structures.description: Bridges the gap at the front between the thyroid and cricoid cartilages. It can be felt just below the Adam’s apple.

structures.label: Conus elasticus
structures.description: An elastic membrane rising from the cricoid toward the vocal folds. Its free upper edge thickens into the vocal ligaments.

structures.label: Vocal ligaments
structures.description: Two bands running from the back of the thyroid cartilage to the arytenoids. With the vocalis muscles they form the vocal folds, which vibrate to make sound.

structures.label: Epiglottic ligaments
structures.description: Tie the epiglottis forward to the hyoid bone and its stalk down to the inside of the thyroid cartilage.

structures.label: Cricothyroid
structures.description: The only intrinsic muscle on the outside of the larynx. It tilts the thyroid cartilage forward, stretching the vocal folds and raising the pitch of the voice.

structures.label: Posterior crico-arytenoid
structures.description: On the back of the cricoid. It is the only muscle that opens the vocal folds, which keeps the airway open for breathing.

structures.label: Lateral crico-arytenoid
structures.description: Rotates the arytenoids inward to bring the vocal folds together.

structures.label: Arytenoid muscles
structures.description: Span the backs of the two arytenoids. They pull the cartilages together to close the back of the glottis.

structures.label: Thyro-arytenoid
structures.description: Runs beside the vocal folds from the thyroid cartilage to the arytenoids. It shortens and relaxes the folds, lowering the pitch.

structures.label: Vocalis
structures.description: The innermost fibres of the thyro-arytenoid, lying along each vocal ligament. They fine-tune the tension of the vocal folds.

structures.label: Aryepiglottic
structures.description: Thin fibres running from the arytenoids up to the sides of the epiglottis. They help narrow the entrance of the larynx when you swallow.

structures.label: Trachea
structures.description: The windpipe. It continues from the cricoid cartilage down into the chest, held open by C-shaped rings of cartilage, and divides into the two main bronchi.

structures.label: Thyroid gland
structures.description: A hormone gland wrapped around the front of the upper trachea. Its isthmus crosses the trachea just below the cricoid cartilage.
